passages.text: Then I saw a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and earth had passed away, and the sea was no more.
passages.sermon:
John saw a new heaven.
John saw a new earth.
The first heaven had passed away.
The first earth had passed away.
The sea no longer existed.
passages.original: Καὶ εἶδον οὐρανὸν καινὸν καὶ γῆν καινήν ὁ γὰρ πρῶτος οὐρανὸς καὶ ἡ πρώτη γῆ ἀπῆλθαν καὶ ἡ θάλασσα οὐκ ἔστιν ἔτι

passages.text: I saw the holy city, the new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.
passages.sermon:
John saw a city.
This city was holy.
This city was called the new Jerusalem.
The city came down from heaven.
God sent the city from heaven.
God prepared the city.
The city was beautiful.
The city was like a bride.
The bride was dressed for her husband.
passages.original: καὶ τὴν πόλιν τὴν ἁγίαν Ἰερουσαλὴμ καινὴν εἶδον καταβαίνουσαν ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἀπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡτοιμασμένην ὡς νύμφην κεκοσμημένην τῷ ἀνδρὶ αὐτῆς

passages.text: And I heard a loud voice from the throne saying: “Behold, the dwelling place of God is with man, and He will dwell with them. They will be His people, and God Himself will be with them as their God.
passages.sermon:
A loud voice spoke from the throne.
The voice said, “Look, God’s dwelling place is now with people.
God will live with them.
They will be His people.
God Himself will be with them.
God will be their God.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἤκουσα φωνῆς μεγάλης ἐκ τοῦ θρόνου λεγούσης Ἰδοὺ ἡ σκηνὴ τοῦ Θεοῦ μετὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων καὶ σκηνώσει μετ’ αὐτῶν καὶ αὐτοὶ λαοὶ αὐτοῦ ἔσονται καὶ αὐτὸς ὁ Θεὸς μετ’ αὐτῶν ἔσται αὐτῶν θεός

passages.text: ‘He will wipe away every tear from their eyes,’ and there will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain, for the former things have passed away.”
passages.sermon:
God will wipe away every tear from their eyes.
There will be no more death.
There will be no more mourning.
There will be no more crying.
There will be no more pain.
The former things have passed away.
passages.original: καὶ ἐξαλείψει πᾶν δάκρυον ἐκ τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν αὐτῶν καὶ ὁ θάνατος οὐκ ἔσται ἔτι οὔτε πένθος οὔτε κραυγὴ οὔτε πόνος οὐκ ἔσται ἔτι ὅτι τὰ πρῶτα ἀπῆλθαν

passages.text: And the One seated on the throne said, “Behold, I make all things new.” Then He said, “Write this down, for these words are faithful and true.”
passages.sermon:
God sat on the throne.
God spoke.
God said, “Look. I make all things new.”
God said, “Write this down.”
God said, “These words are faithful.”
God said, “These words are true.”
passages.original: Καὶ εἶπεν ὁ καθήμενος ἐπὶ τῷ θρόνῳ Ἰδοὺ καινὰ ποιῶ πάντα καὶ λέγει Γράψον ὅτι οὗτοι οἱ λόγοι πιστοὶ καὶ ἀληθινοί εἰσιν

passages.text: And He told me, “It is done! I am the Alpha and the Omega, the Beginning and the End. To the thirsty I will give freely from the spring of the water of life.
passages.sermon:
God sat on the throne.
God spoke to me.
God said, “It is done.”
God said, “I am the Alpha.”
God said, “I am the Omega.”
God is the Beginning.
God is the End.
God said, “I will give to the thirsty.”
God will give water from the spring of life.
God will give this water freely.
passages.original: καὶ εἶπέν μοι Γέγοναν ἐγὼ εἰμι τὸ Ἄλφα καὶ τὸ Ὦ ἡ ἀρχὴ καὶ τὸ τέλος ἐγὼ τῷ διψῶντι δώσω ἐκ τῆς πηγῆς τοῦ ὕδατος τῆς ζωῆς δωρεάν

passages.text: The one who overcomes will inherit all things, and I will be his God, and he will be My son.
passages.sermon:
God sits on the throne.
God speaks with authority.
God promises a reward.
The person who overcomes will inherit all things.
God will be the God of the one who overcomes.
The one who overcomes will be God’s son.
passages.original: ὁ νικῶν κληρονομήσει ταῦτα καὶ ἔσομαι αὐτῷ Θεὸς καὶ αὐτὸς ἔσται μοι υἱός

passages.text: But to the cowardly and unbelieving and abominable and murderers and sexually immoral and sorcerers and idolaters and all liars, their place will be in the lake that burns with fire and sulfur. This is the second death.”
passages.sermon:
God will judge all people.
God will punish certain people.
Cowardly people will face punishment.
Unbelieving people will face punishment.
Abominable people will face punishment.
Murderers will face punishment.
Sexually immoral people will face punishment.
Sorcerers will face punishment.
Idolaters will face punishment.
All liars will face punishment.
Their place will be in the lake that burns with fire and sulfur.
This lake is the second death.
passages.original: Τοῖς δὲ δειλοῖς καὶ ἀπίστοις καὶ ἐβδελυγμένοις καὶ φονεῦσιν καὶ πόρνοις καὶ φαρμάκοις καὶ εἰδωλολάτραις καὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς ψευδέσιν τὸ μέρος αὐτῶν ἐν τῇ λίμνῃ τῇ καιομένῃ πυρὶ καὶ θείῳ ὅ ἐστιν ὁ θάνατος ὁ δεύτερος

passages.text: Then one of the seven angels with the seven bowls full of the seven final plagues came and said to me, “Come, I will show you the bride, the wife of the Lamb.”
passages.sermon:
One of the seven angels came to me.
These seven angels each had a bowl.
Each bowl was full of one of the seven final plagues.
The angel spoke to me.
He said, “Come.”
He said, “I will show you the bride.”
He said, “The bride is the wife of the Lamb.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἦλθεν εἷς ἐκ τῶν ἑπτὰ ἀγγέλων τῶν ἐχόντων τὰς ἑπτὰ φιάλας τῶν γεμόντων τῶν ἑπτὰ πληγῶν τῶν ἐσχάτων καὶ ἐλάλησεν μετ’ ἐμοῦ λέγων Δεῦρο δείξω σοι τὴν νύμφην τὴν γυναῖκα τοῦ ἀρνίου

passages.text: And he carried me away in the Spirit to a mountain great and high, and showed me the holy city of Jerusalem coming down out of heaven from God, shining with the glory of God. Its radiance was like a most precious jewel, like a jasper, as clear as crystal.
passages.sermon:
One of the seven angels carried me away in the Spirit.
He took me to a great and high mountain.
He showed me the holy city.
The city is Jerusalem.
Jerusalem was coming down out of heaven.
God sent this city from Himself.
The city had the glory of God.
The city shone brightly.
Its radiance was like a very precious jewel.
It was like a jasper stone.
It was clear as crystal.
passages.original: Καὶ ἀπήνεγκέν με ἐν Πνεύματι ἐπὶ ὄρος μέγα καὶ ὑψηλόν καὶ ἔδειξέν μοι τὴν πόλιν τὴν ἁγίαν Ἰερουσαλὴμ καταβαίνουσαν ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἀπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἔχουσαν τὴν δόξαν τοῦ Θεοῦ ὁ φωστὴρ αὐτῆς ὅμοιος λίθῳ τιμιωτάτῳ ὡς λίθῳ ἰάσπιδι κρυσταλλίζοντι

passages.text: The city had a great and high wall with twelve gates inscribed with the names of the twelve tribes of Israel, and twelve angels at the gates.
passages.sermon:
The city appeared.
The city had a wall.
The wall was great.
The wall was high.
The city had twelve gates.
Each gate had an angel.
There were twelve angels at the gates.
Each gate had a name written on it.
The names were the names of the twelve tribes of Israel.
passages.original: ἔχουσα τεῖχος μέγα καὶ ὑψηλόν ἔχουσα πυλῶνας δώδεκα καὶ ἐπὶ τοῖς πυλῶσιν ἀγγέλους δώδεκα καὶ ὀνόματα ἐπιγεγραμμένα ἅ ἐστιν τὰ ὀνόματα τῶν δώδεκα φυλῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραήλ

passages.text: There were three gates on the east, three on the north, three on the south, and three on the west.
passages.sermon:
The holy city had gates on every side.
Three gates stood on the east side.
Three gates stood on the north side.
Three gates stood on the south side.
Three gates stood on the west side.
passages.original: ἀπὸ ἀνατολῆς πυλῶνες τρεῖς καὶ ἀπὸ βορρᾶ πυλῶνες τρεῖς καὶ ἀπὸ νότου πυλῶνες τρεῖς καὶ ἀπὸ δυσμῶν πυλῶνες τρεῖς

passages.text: The wall of the city had twelve foundations bearing the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb.
passages.sermon:
The city had a wall.
The wall had twelve foundations.
Each foundation had a name.
The names were the names of the twelve apostles.
The apostles belonged to the Lamb.
passages.original: καὶ τὸ τεῖχος τῆς πόλεως ἔχων θεμελίους δώδεκα καὶ ἐπ’ αὐτῶν δώδεκα ὀνόματα τῶν δώδεκα ἀποστόλων τοῦ Ἀρνίου

passages.text: The angel who spoke with me had a golden measuring rod to measure the city and its gates and walls.
passages.sermon:
An angel spoke with me.
This angel had a golden measuring rod.
The angel used the rod to measure the city.
The angel also measured the gates of the city.
The angel measured the walls of the city.
passages.original: Καὶ ὁ λαλῶν μετ’ ἐμοῦ εἶχεν μέτρον κάλαμον χρυσοῦν ἵνα μετρήσῃ τὴν πόλιν καὶ τοὺς πυλῶνας αὐτῆς καὶ τὸ τεῖχος αὐτῆς

passages.text: The city lies foursquare, with its width the same as its length. And he measured the city with the rod, and all its dimensions were equal—12,000 stadia in length and width and height.
passages.sermon:
The city is a perfect square.
Its length and its width are the same.
The angel measured the city with a rod.
The city is 12,000 stadia long.
The city is 12,000 stadia wide.
The city is 12,000 stadia high.
All its dimensions are equal.
passages.original: καὶ ἡ πόλις τετράγωνος κεῖται καὶ τὸ μῆκος αὐτῆς ὅσον καὶ τὸ πλάτος καὶ ἐμέτρησεν τὴν πόλιν τῷ καλάμῳ ἐπὶ σταδίων δώδεκα χιλιάδων τὸ μῆκος καὶ τὸ πλάτος καὶ τὸ ὕψος αὐτῆς ἴσα ἐστίν

passages.text: And he measured its wall to be 144 cubits, by the human measure the angel was using.
passages.sermon:
An angel spoke with me.
This angel had a golden measuring rod.
The angel measured the city’s wall.
The wall measured 144 cubits.
The angel used a human measurement.
passages.original: καὶ ἐμέτρησεν τὸ τεῖχος αὐτῆς ἑκατὸν τεσσεράκοντα τεσσάρων πηχῶν μέτρον ἀνθρώπου ὅ ἐστιν ἀγγέλου

passages.text: The wall was made of jasper, and the city itself of pure gold, as pure as glass.
passages.sermon: The wall of the city was made of jasper.\r\nThe city itself was made of pure gold.\r\nThe gold was as clear as glass.
passages.original: Καὶ ἡ ἐνδώμησις τοῦ τείχους αὐτῆς ἴασπις καὶ ἡ πόλις χρυσίον καθαρὸν ὅμοιον ὑάλῳ καθαρῷ

passages.text: The foundations of the city walls were adorned with every kind of precious stone: The first foundation was jasper, the second sapphire, the third chalcedony, the fourth emerald, the fifth sardonyx, the sixth carnelian, the seventh chrysolite, the eighth beryl, the ninth topaz, the tenth chrysoprase, the eleventh jacinth, and the twelfth amethyst.
passages.sermon:
The city has walls.
The walls have foundations.
The foundations are decorated with every kind of precious stone.
The first foundation is jasper.
The second foundation is sapphire.
The third foundation is chalcedony.
The fourth foundation is emerald.
The fifth foundation is sardonyx.
The sixth foundation is carnelian.
The seventh foundation is chrysolite.
The eighth foundation is beryl.
The ninth foundation is topaz.
The tenth foundation is chrysoprase.
The eleventh foundation is jacinth.
The twelfth foundation is amethyst.
passages.original: οἱ θεμέλιοι τοῦ τείχους τῆς πόλεως παντὶ λίθῳ τιμίῳ κεκοσμημένοι ὁ θεμέλιος ὁ πρῶτος ἴασπις ὁ δεύτερος σάπφιρος ὁ τρίτος χαλκηδών ὁ τέταρτος σμάραγδος ὁ πέμπτος σαρδόνυξ ὁ ἕκτος σάρδιον ὁ ἕβδομος χρυσόλιθος ὁ ὄγδοος βήρυλλος ὁ ἔνατος τοπάζιον ὁ δέκατος χρυσόπρασος ὁ ἑνδέκατος ὑάκινθος ὁ δωδέκατος ἀμέθυστος

passages.text: And the twelve gates were twelve pearls, with each gate consisting of a single pearl. The main street of the city was pure gold, as clear as glass.
passages.sermon:
The city had twelve gates.
Each gate was a single pearl.
There were twelve pearls in total.
The main street of the city was pure gold.
The gold was as clear as glass.
passages.original: Καὶ οἱ δώδεκα πυλῶνες δώδεκα μαργαρῖται ἀνὰ εἷς ἕκαστος τῶν πυλώνων ἦν ἐξ ἑνὸς μαργαρίτου καὶ ἡ πλατεῖα τῆς πόλεως χρυσίον καθαρὸν ὡς ὕαλος διαυγής

passages.text: But I saw no temple in the city, because the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are its temple.
passages.sermon:
The city had no temple.
I did not see a temple in the city.
The Lord God Almighty is the temple of the city.
The Lamb is also the temple of the city.
passages.original: Καὶ ναὸν οὐκ εἶδον ἐν αὐτῇ ὁ γὰρ Κύριος ὁ Θεὸς ὁ Παντοκράτωρ ναὸς αὐτῆς ἐστιν καὶ τὸ Ἀρνίον

passages.text: And the city has no need of sun or moon to shine on it, because the glory of God illuminates the city, and the Lamb is its lamp.
passages.sermon:
The city does not need the sun.
The city does not need the moon.
The sun and the moon do not shine on the city.
God’s glory gives light to the city.
God is glorious.
The Lamb is the city’s lamp.
The Lamb gives light to the city.
passages.original: καὶ ἡ πόλις οὐ χρείαν ἔχει τοῦ ἡλίου οὐδὲ τῆς σελήνης ἵνα φαίνωσιν αὐτῇ ἡ γὰρ δόξα τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐφώτισεν αὐτήν καὶ ὁ λύχνος αὐτῆς τὸ Ἀρνίον

passages.text: By its light the nations will walk, and into it the kings of the earth will bring their glory.
passages.sermon: The city shines with the light of God and the Lamb.\r\nThe nations walk by this light.\r\nThe kings of the earth bring their glory into the city.
passages.original: καὶ περιπατήσουσιν τὰ ἔθνη διὰ τοῦ φωτὸς αὐτῆς καὶ οἱ βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς φέρουσιν τὴν δόξαν αὐτῶν εἰς αὐτήν

passages.text: Its gates will never be shut at the end of the day, because there will be no night there.
passages.sermon: The city has gates.\r\nThe gates will never be shut during the day.\r\nThere will be no night in the city.
passages.original: καὶ οἱ πυλῶνες αὐτῆς οὐ μὴ κλεισθῶσιν ἡμέρας νὺξ γὰρ οὐκ ἔσται ἐκεῖ

passages.text: And into the city will be brought the glory and honor of the nations.
passages.sermon: The city is holy.\r\nPeople will bring the glory of the nations into the city.\r\nPeople will bring the honor of the nations into the city.
passages.original: Καὶ οἴσουσιν τὴν δόξαν καὶ τὴν τιμὴν τῶν ἐθνῶν εἰς αὐτήν

passages.text: But nothing unclean will ever enter it, nor anyone who practices an abomination or a lie, but only those whose names are written in the Lamb’s Book of Life.
passages.sermon:
The holy city belongs to God and the Lamb.
Nothing unclean will ever enter the city.
No one who does what is shameful will enter.
No one who tells lies will enter.
Only people whose names are written in the Lamb’s Book of Life will enter.
passages.original: καὶ οὐ μὴ εἰσέλθῃ εἰς αὐτὴν πᾶν κοινὸν καὶ ὁ ποιῶν βδέλυγμα καὶ ψεῦδος εἰ μὴ οἱ γεγραμμένοι ἐν τῷ βιβλίῳ τῆς ζωῆς τοῦ Ἀρνίου
